title: Microfrontload GPU Redispatch Experiment - 2026 Q3
summary: Runbook + spreadsheet-style results for a controlled experiment that frontloads small, pre-wired request batches to reduce tail pressure during 5–20 minute microbursts. Focused on redispatching queued work across AZ slices to keep per-GPU utilization below SLO-sensitive thresholds while preserving short-term throughput (tokens/sec).
content:
Purpose:
- Quick experiment doc to test an alternative mitigation: microfrontload + redispatch. Objective is to reduce latency tail and avoid reactive large-scale pre-warming that burns additional capacity.
- This is intentionally lightweight (working sheet) — contains raw observations, CSV-style results, and next-action suggestions.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Typical short microbursts are 75–300s in duration, often concentrated in a single region/az; observed in June–July 2026 telemetry.
- Average token length per request for the burst cohort = 360 tokens (median 210).
- Our baseline per-GPU soft-util target for SLOs is 68% sustained; we allow spikes to 82% for up to 30s.
- GPU types in the experiment: A100-40, H100-80, L40; we include a T4 pool for low-cost embeddings fallback.
- Prewiring: maintain tiny (2–4) pre-established concurrent prefixes/KV caches per worker to reduce first-token latency when redispatched.

Experiment scenarios (labels):
- A: baseline (no microfrontload, standard prewarm heuristics on 5-min thresholds).
- B: microfrontload enabled (15s pre-batch sent to warm hot-pool; redispatch allowed across AZs within 80ms RTT window).
- C: aggressive redispatch (cross-region allowed up to 250ms with quantized fallback model variant).

Observations (raw):
- Scenario B reduced 95th latency for burst cohort by ~18% vs A, with a 9% higher short-term tokens/sec (per-pool).
- Scenario C gave additional throughput but increased cross-region egress events by 3.8% and incurred cold-cache penalties for ~4% of requests.
- Prewiring KV prefixes reduced attach-time variance; when present, redispatch routing success rate rose from 71% -> 92%.
- Cost delta (infra) for B vs A estimated: +2.1% in effective GPU-hours (due to more modest warm-pools kept active), but 12% reduction in emergency pre-warms over 24h.

Operational controls and config knobs tried in the experiment:
- redispatch.max_rtt_ms = 80 (B) or 250 (C)
- prewarm.batch_lead_s = 15
- pool.soft_util_target_pct = 70 (A) -> adjusted to 68 for H100 pool because of thermal throttling trends
- kv.cache_slots_per_worker = 3
- fallback_model_variant = quant4x (smaller memory, lower perf quality)

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Need A/B on user-perceived quality for quant4x fallback under scenario C (ticket JIRA-ML-4425).
- Confirm networking cost model for cross-region redispatch; involve finance for a delta estimate.
- Validate behavior under non-uniform token-size distributions (we tested with median 210; heavy-long tails may change prewarm economics).

Recommended headroom policy (working):
- For AZ-sliced pools: keep soft target util at model-family-specific value (H100: 66–68%, A100: 68–72%, L40: 62–66%) and maintain a dynamic microfrontload budget equal to 6–9% of pool capacity during expected burst windows.
- When observable burst probability > 12% in last 3 hours for an AZ, enable microfrontload for that AZ only (avoid fleet-wide churn).
- Set redispatch.max_rtt_ms = 100 as default; increase to 200 only for controlled experiments with compensating egress accounting.

Action items (next week):
- Infra: roll B config to canary (us-west1 + eu-west1) for 72h, monitor 95th/99th latency and emergency pre-warms. Owner: Lucas Moreno.
- ML: run quality evaluation for quant4x fallback on top-10 customer prompts. Owner: Emily Zhang.
- Finance: quick delta estimate for cross-region egress and prewarm savings. Owner: Priya Patel.
- Run synthetic stressbench for long-tail token distribution on staging H100 fleet. Owner: Noah Stein.

Notes and provenance:
- Data used: sampled telemetry from 2026-06-20 -> 2026-07-09 (internal: telemetry-sample-2026-06-20.tar.gz).
- Experiment run ids: exp-mf-2026-07-16-b (scenario B), exp-mf-2026-07-17-c (scenario C).
- Related runbooks and reading: confluence.redwood/microfrontload-runbook (draft), ops-playbook/redispatch-guidelines (WIP).

Slack snippets (copied raw during run):
- "B looks promising — 95th down, but cross-region bump visible" — #infra-ops (Lucas)
- "we should gate C until quant fallback policy validated" — #ml-eng (Emily)

Quick conclusion (working):
- Microfrontload + conservative redispatch looks like a viable middle ground for reducing tail latency in short microbursts without resorting to fleet-wide aggressive prewarm. Requires careful egress accounting and a small quality assessment for fallback variants.
